source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-14: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 14 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat this as a provisional cluster_performance analysis for RoCE variant 14. Assume a multi-node GPU collective workload, but do not assume RoCE is lossless, GPU-direct is active, routes are symmetric, or a fallback transport is absent. Separate measured facts, estimates, and unknowns. Inventory GPU/NIC/switch-port topology, PCIe/NVLink affinity, firmware/driver/library versions, MTU, link speed, VLAN/priority mapping, queue-pair count, message-size/concurrency distributions, clocks, and transport selection. Trace the path from collective calls through verbs work requests/completions and registered host/GPU buffers to NIC, fabric, and peer; correlate application timing with NIC and switch counters rather than treating either as a causal proof.

Falsifiable hypothesis and test: under fixed placement, software, workload, warm-up, and sample count, interleave a matched baseline with the suspected path/configuration. The change is supported only if p95 and p99 collective latency improve by at least 10% (report ms or us and confidence intervals) without worsening p99 step time, timeout/retry/error rate, drops, pause duration, ECN marks, completion errors, or correctness. Compare distributions, not just means, and stratify by message size and route. Check MTU consistency, route symmetry, PFC priority and pause behavior, ECN marking, congestion, NIC queue/counter telemetry, and fallback evidence.

For the design/performance decision, specify the intended topology, priority and MTU contract, route symmetry, queue and completion behavior, GPU-direct versus host-staging path, congestion controls, observability, and fallback policy. Define capacity/headroom and tail-latency SLOs with units and workload strata, then validate with interleaved baselines and fault-injection tests. Keep rollback and correctness gates explicit; a design is not accepted from model reasoning alone.

Rollback or failure condition: stop the canary and restore the last known-good configuration if p99 latency rises by more than 10%, timeout/retry or completion errors increase, pause/drop/ECN signals exceed the baseline confidence bound, links flap, or collective correctness fails. Evidence required before claiming improvement: topology and route inventory, MTU/priority/PFC/ECN configuration, transport/fallback trace, synchronized application/verbs/NIC/switch telemetry, matched raw samples with uncertainty, and correctness plus rollback logs.
risks: RoCE losslessness, topology, GPU-direct behavior, and fallback are platform-dependent and unverified.
Counters may not explain end-to-end tails without synchronized correlation.
A mitigation can worsen pauses, drops, retries, or correctness if applied without a canary.

interleaved matched baseline with raw percentile distributions by message size and route
synchronized application, verbs, NIC, switch, queue, pause, ECN, error, and link telemetry
correctness checks and canary rollback logs

Use synchronized timestamps and packet/path or queue evidence to distinguish congestion, priority misconfiguration, MTU/path mismatch, asymmetric routing, queue starvation, and fallback from application stragglers. Do not disable safety controls globally or infer causality from a single run.

Rollback or failure condition: stop the canary and restore the last known-good configuration if p99 latency rises by more than 10%, timeout/retry or completion errors increase, pause/drop/ECN signals exceed the baseline confidence bound, links flap, or collective correctness fails. Evidence required before claiming improvement: topology and route inventory, MTU/priority/PFC/ECN configuration, transport/fallback trace, synchronized application/verbs/NIC/switch telemetry, matched raw samples with uncertainty, and correctness plus rollback logs.
risks: RoCE losslessness, topology, GPU-direct behavior, and fallback are platform-dependent and unverified.
Counters may not explain end-to-end tails without synchronized correlation.
A mitigation can worsen pauses, drops, retries, or correctness if applied without a canary.
evidence_required: topology, route, MTU, priority, PFC/ECN, firmware, and transport inventory
interleaved matched baseline with raw percentile distributions by message size and route
synchronized application, verbs, NIC, switch, queue, pause, ECN, error, and link telemetry
correctness checks and canary rollback logs
